claims.text: High physical activity was associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR: 0.76 [95% CI: 0.74-0.79]).
High physical activity was associated with lower risk of composite CVD mortality (HR: 0.74 [95% CI: 0.70-0.77]).
High physical activity was associated with lower risk of incident composite CVD (HR: 0.90 [95% CI: 0.88-0.92]).
High diet quality was associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR: 0.81 [95% CI: 0.77-0.85]).
High diet quality was associated with lower risk of composite CVD mortality (HR: 0.81 [95% CI: 0.75-0.88]).
High diet quality was associated with lower risk of incident composite CVD (HR: 0.87 [95% CI: 0.84-0.90]).
Physical activity showed nonlinear associations with outcomes, plateauing at approximately 2,500 metabolic equivalent min/wk.
High physical activity combined with high diet quality was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.64 [95% CI: 0.60-0.68]).
High physical activity combined with high diet quality was associated with lower composite CVD mortality (HR: 0.61 [95% CI: 0.54-0.68]).
High physical activity combined with high diet quality was associated with lower incident composite CVD (HR: 0.83 [95% CI: 0.79-0.88]).
Significant multiplicative interactions between physical activity and diet quality were observed for stroke mortality, composite CVD, and heart failure.
Joint associations of physical activity and diet quality with outcomes were stronger at more advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages.

evidence.description: High PA was associated with lower risks of all-cause mortality (HR: 0.76 [95% CI: 0.74-0.79]).
High PA was associated with lower composite CVD mortality (0.74 [0.70-0.77]).
High PA was associated with incident composite CVD (0.90 [0.88-0.92]).
For high diet quality, corresponding HR (95% CI) for all-cause mortality was 0.81 (0.77-0.85).
For high diet quality, composite CVD mortality HR was 0.81 (0.75-0.88).
For high diet quality, incident composite CVD HR was 0.87 (0.84-0.90).
PA showed nonlinear associations with these outcomes, plateauing at approximately 2,500 metabolic equivalent min/wk.
High PA combined with high diet quality showed inverse associations with all-cause mortality (0.64 [0.60-0.68]).
High PA combined with high diet quality showed composite CVD mortality HR of 0.61 (0.54-0.68).
High PA combined with high diet quality showed incident composite CVD HR of 0.83 (0.79-0.88).
Significant multiplicative interactions between PA and diet quality were observed for stroke mortality, composite CVD, and heart failure.
The joint associations with these outcomes were stronger at more advanced CKM syndrome stages.

methodologies.name: Cox proportional hazards modeling
methodologies.description: Cox proportional hazards models assessed independent and joint associations of physical activity and diet quality with incident CVD, cause-specific CVD mortality, and all-cause mortality across CKM stages.
conditions: PA categorized as high (≥150 min/wk of walking or moderate-to-vigorous activity) or low
Diet quality classified as low, median, or high

limitations.text: Physical activity and diet quality associations within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework remained previously unexplored.
